reproduction_target: panREPET: a reference-free Snakemake pipeline that detects TE insertions shared between de novo assembled genomes of a species by pairwise comparison. Applied to a Brachypodium distachyon pan-genome (54 -> 42 accessions after QC). Steps: TE reference-library build (TEdenovo/REPET on Bd21 v3.2) and TE annotation (panTEannot, a Snakemake re-implementation of REPET TEannot via Blaster/Censor/RepeatMasker packaged in TE_finder); then panREPET proper: coverage-based TE-copy extraction (covcons/extractCopies.py), flanking-sequence extension (bedtools slop), reciprocal-best-hit detection (Minimap2 + Matcher/te_finder), clique detection (NetworkX find_cliques), phylogenetic-distance computation (Biopython Phylo), and downstream ecogenome/climate statistics (Seaborn/statsmodels, kgc R package).
granularity_note: Stage-2 line-level code-check of two author repos on ForgeMIA GitLab (git clone --depth 1, env/workflow/container files only; NO data downloaded): panREPET (Snakefile, Snakefile_singularity, envs/*.yaml, containers/panREPET.def, config/example.yaml, containers/.gitlab-ci.yml) and panTEannot (workflow/Snakefile, workflow/config/config_Bd.yaml, containers/how_install_te-finder.txt). Coarse one-step-per-named-tool granularity from Stage-1 preserved. Code-check confirms: (a) reproducibility rests on per-rule bare conda specs (envs/*.yaml) with top-level version pins only and a floating 'python >= 3.5', no channel/build lock, no transitive closure, and tefinder.yaml carries NO version at all; (b) the container is referenced ONLY by mutable tags across three locations (README 'library://jconfais/repet/panrepet:1.0'; config/example.yaml 'oras://registry.forge.inrae.fr/urgi/urgi-anagen/panrepet:v1.0.0'; containers/README ':cicd'/':v1.0.0') with NO content digest anywhere; (c) containers/panREPET.def is a build-from-recipe with a floating base image (debian:11-slim tag), 'conda update -n base --all -y' (fully floating), a git clone '--branch dev-2.32.1' of te_finder (mutable branch, not a commit), and a version mismatch vs the conda envs (def pins networkx=2.5.1 while envs/networkX.yaml pins networkx=2.4) — so it is not a static lock and not even internally consistent. No external DB/reference is fetched in code: all genome assemblies, the TE consensus library and the RepetDB/TEdenovo library are supplied as pre-existing LOCAL file paths in config (example.yaml uses data/ files; panTEannot config_Bd.yaml uses absolute /mnt/... paths). No wet-lab steps (public de novo assemblies reused), so W=0.

steps.label: TE reference-library build with TEdenovo (REPET v3.0, Flutre et al. 2011) from the Bd21 v3.2 genome; library also distributed via RepetDB. REPET v3.0 named in panREPET README prose but this pipeline is NOT in either repo (library supplied as a pre-built data/ fasta); no REPET lock

panTEannot TE annotation (Snakemake re-implementation of REPET TEannot; Blaster/Censor/RepeatMasker packaged inside TE_finder). Code-check: workflow/Snakefile uses 'singularity: TE_finder' and config_Bd.yaml + containers/how_install_te-finder.txt pin te_finder 2.31 (library://hquesneville/default/te_finder:2.31, tag-only sif) — a code-level version pin, but tag-only container with no digest and no conda lock

panREPET Step 1: extract TE copies by coverage percentage (extractCopies.py; cov_consensus param) - conda env envs/biopython.yaml (biopython=1.79, python>=3.5 floating), cov_consensus set in config/example.yaml (0.95)

panREPET Step 2: add flanking genomic sequence via bedtools slop (extendGFF rule) - envs/bedtools.yaml pins bedtools=2.30.0 (no build string, no python pin); also bundled in the tag-only Singularity image

panREPET Step 3: bidirectional (reciprocal) best-hit detection via Minimap2 (minimap2 rule + launchMinimap2.py) then Matcher (matcher rule) - envs/minimap2.yaml pins minimap2=2.24 (python>=3.5 floating); Matcher provided only inside the tag-only Singularity image (README says 'matcher'; the .def actually builds blaster2.32/te_finder dev-2.32.1) - no standalone Matcher version, image-vs-README tool naming ambiguity

panREPET Step 4: TE-insertion clique detection with NetworkX (cliques.py: read_edgelist + find_cliques). Code-check CONFIRMS envs/networkX.yaml pins networkx=2.4 in the conda env (Stage-1 believed it was prose-only). NOTE: containers/panREPET.def pins networkx=2.5.1 - conda-env vs container version MISMATCH
Phylogenetic pairwise-distance computation between accessions using the Biopython Phylo module (biopython=1.79 pinned in envs/biopython.yaml and envs/minimap2.yaml; python>=3.5 floating)

Downstream ecogenome/climate statistics and figures: clustermaps (Seaborn), ANOVA (statsmodels, python 3.10.13), climate-class assignment (kgc R package v1.0.0.2). Code-check: NO analysis/figure/stat scripts present in either repo (panREPET stats.py only emits clique stats); Seaborn/statsmodels/kgc not in any env file

No step exceeds RI: the environment is NOT statically locked — the Singularity image is referenced only by mutable tags (:1.0 / :v1.0.0 / :cicd) with no content digest, the envs/*.yaml are bare conda specs (floating python>=3.5, no build strings, no transitive closure, tefinder unversioned), and containers/panREPET.def is a build-recipe with a floating base, 'conda update --all', a mutable git branch clone, and an internal networkx version mismatch (2.4 vs 2.5.1).
headline.coverage: 8 computational steps assessed from two author Snakemake repos (panREPET + panTEannot) at line level plus biorxiv v2 Methods prose. No wet-lab steps (public de novo assemblies reused), so W=0.

gaps.where: Whole pipeline environment (panREPET: Snakefile conda directives + Singularity image + panREPET.def; panTEannot: TE_finder image)
gaps.missing: No statically-complete environment lock exists. (1) Container referenced ONLY by mutable tags in three places (README library://jconfais/repet/panrepet:1.0; config/example.yaml oras://registry.forge.inrae.fr/urgi/urgi-anagen/panrepet:v1.0.0; containers/README :cicd) with NO @sha256 / content digest. (2) envs/*.yaml are bare conda specs: top-level version pins (biopython=1.79, bedtools=2.30.0, minimap2=2.24, networkx=2.4) but 'python >= 3.5' floating, no channels lock beyond conda-forge/bioconda, no build strings, no transitive closure; tefinder.yaml has NO version at all. (3) containers/panREPET.def is a build-from-recipe with floating base debian:11-slim, 'conda update -n base --all -y', a mutable 'git clone --branch dev-2.32.1' of te_finder, and pins networkx=2.5.1 (conflicting with envs/networkX.yaml networkx=2.4). None of these is a conda-lock/pixi/renv lockfile or a digest-pinned image.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a resolved lockfile (conda-lock or pixi.lock) covering interpreter+channels+platform+transitive deps for every rule, AND/OR pin the Singularity image by content digest (SIF sha256 / OCI @sha256) instead of a tag, then have Stage-2 execution validate the capture. Reconcile the networkx 2.4 vs 2.5.1 discrepancy.

gaps.where: C1 TEdenovo/REPET, C2 panTEannot (TE_finder/Blaster/Censor/RepeatMasker), and Matcher (C5)
gaps.missing: REPET v3.0 (C1) is named in README prose only and its pipeline is not in either repo (library supplied as a pre-built fasta). TE_finder 2.31 (C2) is pinned in config/how_install but via a tag-only sif; the RepeatMasker/Censor sub-tool versions inside TE_finder are not surfaced. Matcher (C5) is named in the README but the .def actually builds blaster2.32 (te_finder dev-2.32.1) — a naming/version ambiguity with no standalone Matcher version. Downstream Seaborn/statsmodels/kgc (C8) versions absent.
gaps.how_to_close: Record exact versions/builds for all REPET-family tools (and the RepeatMasker/library versions inside TE_finder) and the downstream Python/R plotting-stats packages in a versions table or lockfile; disambiguate Matcher vs blaster/te_finder.

gaps.where: Input genome assemblies and TE library (Data availability) — supplied as local paths, not fetched in code
gaps.missing: The executable workflow obtains NO external DB in code: config/example.yaml points to bundled data/ files and panTEannot config_Bd.yaml points to absolute /mnt/Volume_Somia/... paths. Provenance of the 53 B. distachyon de novo assemblies (Phytozome, generic https://phytozome.jgi.doe.gov/, Gordon et al. 2017), BdTR7a (Stritt et al. 2019) and the Bd21 TE library (RepetDB / TEdenovo) is prose-only, with no versioned accession, release tag, or checksum in code.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide an explicit accession/version table (or a deposited snapshot/DOI) for every genome assembly and the exact RepetDB/TEdenovo TE-library release, and reference those pinned identifiers from the workflow config.

gaps.missing: RepetDB (urgi.versailles.inrae.fr/repetdb) and Phytozome are live, versioned-over-time databases with no pinned snapshot in code; retrieval is not deterministic. The generic Phytozome URL in the paper/README fails to resolve (000; content migrated to phytozome-next.jgi.doe.gov).
gaps.how_to_close: Record the database release/date-stamped export used, or deposit the retrieved TE library and genome set as a fixed archive (Zenodo/figshare) with a DOI.
